wrong_answer_semantics: B asserts that the second 4 by 4 black-white tile cannot be formed. It is constructible with the L unchanged and the square rotated three quarter-turns, as the independent exhaustive witness records. The formal unique impossible tile remains E.
mechanism: Red exterior brackets identify the genuine L placement on the top and left of B. Blue brackets compare the bottom edge of the remaining 3 by 3 square to the separate source square. Predicted error: preserve the zero rotation suggested by the two red arm matches for both pieces, reject the blue square pattern mismatch, and declare B impossible. In reality L needs zero rotation and the square three quarter-turns; separate pieces are free to move independently.

material_difference_from_all_known_prior: Old wrong_corner_L_transfer tested an unsuitable C corner (preset C, D/A finals). Current p01 compared only the square and the lower-left region of A (preset A, C/B finals). This new hypothesis compares both independently movable pieces at the actual B assembly: a full two-arm L match and a complementary three-cell square edge. The potential error is propagating the red piece orientation to the other piece, not repeating the old C reflection or merely changing the square-only A target.
human_semantics_before_visual_review: Every added mark is outside the material with a nonzero gap and short perpendicular end caps: an external dimension/comparison bracket, not transported colored edging. Original grids, all unit-cell fills, all source/option boundaries and labels are untouched. The 4 independent brackets are open; no interior partition, closed region or third area-bearing piece is drawn. Under physical paper/ink reading all shown material remains exactly the original black-white material. Actual image still requires primary visual review before calls.
